title: Short-Circuit Evaluation
definition: Short-circuit evaluation stops evaluating a compound Boolean expression when the final result is already determined.
purpose: Explain conditional operand evaluation and its correctness, safety, and side-effect consequences.
history: Many programming languages implement conditional logical operators that avoid unnecessary or unsafe right-operand evaluation.
mental_model: The left answer may make the right question irrelevant, so the right expression is never visited.
analogy: A locked outer door makes checking an inner badge unnecessary; the analogy fails because JavaScript logical operators may return operand values rather than Boolean values.
industry_notes: Use short-circuiting for explicit guards or value selection, not as a substitute for readable control flow when effects are involved.
ai_notes: AI often overlooks valid falsy values and skipped effects in shorthand expressions.
interview_notes: Ask for the returned value and evaluation trace, not only truthiness.
